title: Impersonation during account registration
description: An attacker could impersonate the Homeowner during the account registration process, potentially gaining unauthorized access to the Home Hub system and enrolling cameras/sensors under false pretenses.
assumptions: The registration process relies on credentials that can be compromised or forged.

title: Disclosure of personal information during registration
description: Sensitive personal information provided by the Homeowner during account registration (e.g., name, address, contact details) could be disclosed to unauthorized parties during transmission or storage.
assumptions: The registration data is transmitted over potentially insecure channels or stored without adequate protection.

title: Linkability of homeowner activities across devices
description: The Home Hub could link the Homeowner's account registration with camera/sensor enrollment data, potentially creating a comprehensive profile of the homeowner's security system usage and location patterns.
assumptions: The Home Hub maintains logs or databases that correlate different aspects of the homeowner's interaction with the system.

title: Guest Presence Detection via Access Code Entry
description: An observer can detect that a guest is attempting to access the home by observing the guest entering an access code at the Home Hub. This reveals the guest's presence and intent to enter, even without accessing the actual code.
assumptions: Observer has line-of-sight to the Home Hub or can observe system responses (lights, sounds, etc.)

title: Access Code Observation/Shoulder Surfing
description: The temporary access code entered by the guest could be observed by bystanders standing nearby, or captured through recording devices, leading to unauthorized access to the home.
assumptions: Guest enters code in visible location; no physical protection of input

title: Linkability of Guest Access Events
description: An observer could link multiple access code entries to the same guest or time period, potentially building a profile of guest visitation patterns and habits.
assumptions: System logs or observable patterns allow correlation of access events

title: Code Reuse/Usurpation by Unauthorized Parties
description: If the temporary access code is observed or leaked, an unauthorized party could reuse it to gain access to the home, effectively usurping the guest's legitimate access.
assumptions: Code is not sufficiently randomized or time-limited; no additional authentication required

title: Linkability of Event Patterns
description: An attacker with access to the local event log could link multiple motion/door/sensor events together to reconstruct detailed patterns of household activity, including occupancy schedules, routine behaviors, and presence/absence patterns.
assumptions: Attacker has physical or network access to the local event log storage
uncertainty_note: Tree node L.1.1 is a reasonable fit for linkability at the data store level

title: Identification of Individuals from Event Data
description: Motion, door, and sensor events could be used to identify specific individuals or their presence in the home, potentially revealing who is present, when they enter/leave, and their movement patterns within the house.
assumptions: Event data contains sufficient detail to infer individual presence or identity
uncertainty_note: I.1.1 is a reasonable fit for identification at the data store level

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Event Log
description: The local event log containing motion/door/sensor events could be accessed by unauthorized parties, potentially through physical access, network compromise, or insecure storage mechanisms, leading to disclosure of sensitive household activity data.
assumptions: Event log is not adequately protected against unauthorized access
uncertainty_note: D.1.1 is a reasonable fit for disclosure at the data store level

title: Data Manipulation of Event Log
description: An attacker with access to the local event log could alter, delete, or inject false events, compromising the integrity and authenticity of the recorded household activity data.
assumptions: Event log lacks adequate access controls and integrity protection
uncertainty_note: Dd.1.1 is a reasonable fit for data manipulation at the data store level

title: Identifiability of individuals in camera footage
description: Camera clips uploaded to cloud storage contain identifiable information about individuals in the home environment, including faces, activities, and personal behaviors.
assumptions: Camera footage captures identifiable individuals; cloud storage is accessible to authorized parties.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of video data
description: Cloud video storage may be vulnerable to unauthorized access, data breaches, or improper access controls, leading to disclosure of sensitive camera footage to unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Cloud storage provider has security vulnerabilities or insufficient access controls.

title: Linkability of video data across sessions
description: Camera clips uploaded over time can be linked to specific individuals, events, or time periods, potentially enabling profiling or tracking of individuals' activities.
assumptions: Multiple video uploads can be correlated; metadata or timestamps allow linking.

title: Usurpation of cloud storage access
description: Unauthorized actors may gain access to cloud video storage and impersonate legitimate users, potentially accessing or manipulating stored camera footage.
assumptions: Authentication mechanisms may be compromised; cloud storage access controls are insufficient.

title: Excessive motion data disclosure to backend
description: Home Hub (P1) forwards real-time motion alert data to Mobile App Backend (P2). If motion data contains personally identifiable information (e.g., timestamps, location patterns, activity logs), this constitutes a data disclosure across a process boundary. The minimality principle may be violated if the data shared exceeds what's strictly necessary for the mobile app's functionality.
assumptions: Motion data may contain personal information that can be linked to individuals or households
uncertainty_note: Using Dd.4 from context [5] as it addresses excessive exposure of personal data to known parties at design time

title: Linkability of motion alerts to individuals
description: Motion alert data transmitted from Home Hub to Mobile App Backend could be linked to specific individuals or households based on timing, frequency, and location patterns. This linkability threat exists at the source (P1) where the data originates.
assumptions: Motion data patterns can be correlated with individual presence or behavior
uncertainty_note: Tree node L.1 is standard LINDDUN Pro node for linkability at source position

title: Linkability of Aggregated Analytics Data
description: Aggregated device-usage analytics shared with cloud vendor may contain patterns or metadata that could be linked with other datasets to re-identify individual users or correlate with other privacy-sensitive information.
assumptions: Vendor has access to additional data sources that could be combined with this analytics data
uncertainty_note: Using L.1.1 based on general LINDDUN methodology; exact node may vary by context

title: Unauthorized Disclosure to Third Parties
description: Cloud analytics vendor may share or resell the aggregated device-usage analytics with third parties without proper authorization or consent from the original data subjects.
assumptions: Vendor has contractual obligations that may not be fully enforced or monitored
uncertainty_note: D.1.1 selected as representative disclosure threat node

title: Unauthorized Use of Analytics Data
description: Cloud analytics vendor may use the shared device-usage analytics for purposes beyond the agreed scope, such as profiling, targeted advertising, or selling to data brokers.
assumptions: Vendor's business model may incentivize broader data utilization than originally specified
uncertainty_note: U.1.1 selected as representative usurpation threat node

title: Data Manipulation of Analytics Results
description: Cloud analytics vendor may alter, filter, or manipulate the aggregated device-usage analytics data before processing or reporting, potentially affecting downstream decision-making or compliance reporting.
assumptions: Vendor has technical capability to modify data and may do so without proper audit trails
uncertainty_note: Dd.1.1 selected as representative data manipulation threat node
